invariants: Sixteen independent literal observations execute the actual pinned and native engines: durable ranking/pages, unchanged revisions, events, relevant and global cursor generations, live preference, literal operators, empty availability, one stable retry, instability refusal, provider withdrawal/replacement, pre-abort and closed refusal.

The canonical session-query-sqlite package resolves to the modern FTS engine. Three real Web profile/preset consumers assert its identity and perform Remote searches before and after durable reload, including both original and forked sessions.
One shared readiness operation owns the modern connection. Caller abort does not cancel shared readiness or release serial ownership while an abort-ignoring dependency is still running.

Before/after durable snapshot tokens, detached inspections and live identities must stabilize within exactly two observations. Provider replacement forces fresh inspection even when revisions collide; withdrawal hides durable rows without deleting their physical index.

One real SQLite transaction atomically publishes main/TEMP documents, session generations and the global generation; a failed publication rolls back both indexes and a subsequent search remains usable.
Close refuses newly queued work, drains accepted work and shared readiness, and closes the owned connection once. Optional provider child cleanup drains before retirement.

Actual extracted observations require Python 3.8.10, the candidate's engine module/root and its hash-pinned SQLite 3.51.2 source identity. Missing, foreign, malformed or changed observations are refused.
identity: Cursor identity combines an engine instance, sessions/events scope, normalized request fingerprint and relevant generation. This contract measures declared ASCII filter identities; general ICU collation remains open.
ownership: Engine owns shared readiness, serial queue, private main/TEMP database and optional persistence injection; persistence and live sessions retain their own lifetimes.
ordering: Validate and capture request, observe cancellation, await serial ownership/readiness, stabilize detached corpus, atomically publish, validate cursor and select ranked FTS rows.
errors: Typed invalid-config/request/cursor, stale-cursor, aborted, persistence-failed and index-failed boundaries retain original failure causes in the declared cases, including readiness's signal-dependent non-Error adaptation.
cancellation: Pre-abort performs no provider observation/open; queued abort cannot permit overlap with accepted dependency cleanup; close drains accepted work and refuses queued work.
adaptation: Python tasks and the private official Windows SQLite C API implement the declared source asynchronous ownership and STRICT/FTS boundary without Node in the portable runtime.
open_questions: CON-SESSION-QUERY-UNICODE defines the new ICU request identity extension; its complete candidate acceptance is pending. Full Unicode regex/extraction and all locales remain outside these bounded contracts.
Exhaustive event extraction, all concurrent binding/index histories, public tool/package ABI, very large histories and SQLite canonical schema-19 storage remain separate.
The rejected 24f9f83d original-browser startup cancellation remains independently unrooted. FTS acceptance cannot mark it fixed.
Windows ACL, cross-process/power-loss and actual Win7 certification remain outside this bounded contract; real Win7 is deferred by the user.
